title: Contrast and tension in a speech
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which two opposites does your talk hold in tension?
I said that last time I talked about alliteration, and that this time I would talk about symmetry in a speech, such as a tongue twister, where the sounds balance.
I said I would introduce concepts used in speeches, and asked whether that would be useful.
I said that dialectical tension and contrast are two concepts that are very good in politics: the yin and yang, black and white, two opposing views like a tug of war.
I asked what your stance should be when speaking to the masses in the middle of that tug of war, and a student answered that you identify your audience and the goal.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write two opposites in your message.
Write the sentence that holds both.
Write a line with matched sounds.
Write who is on each side of the rope.
Write where you stand and why.

check.q: What did I say last time's device was?
What is dialectical tension, as I described it?
choices: Two opposing views like a tug of war

check.q: What did a student say to identify?

recap: Use contrast and tension, with an audience and a goal.
